(function() {
    function attachCookieButtonHandler() {
        var cookieSettingsButton = document.getElementById("view-cookie-settings");
        if (!cookieSettingsButton) {
            return false;
        }
        
        // Check if handler already attached
        if (cookieSettingsButton.hasAttribute("data-handler-attached")) {
            return true;
        }
        
        cookieSettingsButton.setAttribute("data-handler-attached", "true");
        
        cookieSettingsButton.addEventListener("click", function(e) {
            e.preventDefault();
            e.stopPropagation();
            
            // Function to try opening CookieControl
            function openCookieControl(retryCount) {
                retryCount = retryCount || 0;
                var maxRetries = 30; // Try for up to 3 seconds
                
                if (typeof CookieControl !== "undefined") {
                    // Method 1: Try CookieControl.show() - this is the standard method
                    if (typeof CookieControl.show === "function") {
                        try {
                            CookieControl.show();
                            return;
                        } catch (err) {
                            console.error("CookieControl.show() error:", err);
                        }
                    }
                    
                    // Method 2: Try to find and click CookieControl built-in settings link/button
                    // CookieControl creates a settings link - try various selectors
                    var selectors = [
                        "a[href*=\"#cookie\" i]",
                        "button[aria-label*=\"cookie\" i]",
                        "button[aria-label*=\"preference\" i]",
                        ".cc-c-settings",
                        ".CookieControlSettings",
                        "[data-cc-event=\"click:show\"]",
                        "a.cc-settings",
                        "button.cc-settings"
                    ];
                    
                    for (var s = 0; s < selectors.length; s++) {
                        var ccButton = document.querySelector(selectors[s]);
                        if (ccButton) {
                            try {
                                ccButton.click();
                                return;
                            } catch (err) {
                                // Try next selector
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    
                    // Method 3: Try to trigger via the corner button (if layout is SLIDEOUT)
                    var cornerButton = document.querySelector(".cc-c-corner, .CookieControlCorner");
                    if (cornerButton) {
                        try {
                            cornerButton.click();
                            return;
                        } catch (err) {
                            // Continue to next method
                        }
                    }
                    
                    // Method 4: Try other possible API methods
                    var methods = ["open", "openSettings", "showSettings", "toggle"];
                    for (var i = 0; i < methods.length; i++) {
                        if (typeof CookieControl[methods[i]] === "function") {
                            try {
                                CookieControl[methods[i]]();
                                return;
                            } catch (err) {
                                // Try next method
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    
                    // Debug: Log whats available
                    if (retryCount === 0) {
                        console.log("CookieControl object:", CookieControl);
                        console.log("CookieControl methods:", Object.keys(CookieControl).filter(function(key) {
                            return typeof CookieControl[key] === "function";
                        }));
                    }
                }
                
                // Retry if not ready yet
                if (retryCount < maxRetries) {
                    setTimeout(function() {
                        openCookieControl(retryCount + 1);
                    }, 100);
                } else {
                    console.error("Failed to open CookieControl after " + (maxRetries * 100) + "ms. CookieControl available:", typeof CookieControl !== "undefined");
                }
            }
            
            openCookieControl();
        });
        
        return true;
    }
    
    // Initialize when DOM is ready
    if (document.readyState === "loading") {
        document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function() {
            // Wait a bit for CookieControl to initialize
            setTimeout(attachCookieButtonHandler, 500);
        });
    } else {
        // DOM already loaded, but wait for CookieControl
        setTimeout(attachCookieButtonHandler, 500);
    }
})();

<div class="rich-text">

<h2 id="arrival-152532-title" class="h2">
                                          Arrival
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>The closest station is Royal Victoria Dock on the Docklands Light Railway, this station has step-free access.   </p>
<p>Canning Town station also has step-free access, this links to Royal Victoria via the Jubilee Line and local bus routes.  </p>
<p>Please see visit the <a data-entity-substitution="canonical" data-entity-type="node" data-entity-uuid="8e58ac42-8cd6-4a10-b83c-58af997cc9ee" href="/who-we-are/city-halls-buildings-and-squares/how-find-city-hall" title="How to find City Hall">How to find City Hall</a> webpage for further information on travel options.  </p>
<p>The Transport for London website provides information on <a href="https://tfl.gov.uk/transport-accessibility/plan-an-accessible-journey">how to plan accessible travel</a> around London.</p>
<p>The <a href="http://www.accessable.co.uk/">AccessAble website</a> provides further information about the accessibility of stations around London that can be useful when planning your journey to City Hall.</p>

  </div>

<h2 id="access-and-security-152534-title" class="h2">
                                          Access and security
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>The visitor entrance to City Hall is located the the front of the building, with level access from the street. All public areas including the Chamber, Committee Rooms, cafe and event space is located on the ground floor.  </p>
<p>For the safety of all visitors and staff, visitors pass through an airport style security search area upon arrival. Once inside, the reception area is clearly visible. </p>
<p>Security and reception officers are trained to consider wellbeing issues to ensure the safety, physical and emotional comfort of visitors to City Hall.  </p>
<h3 id="guideassistance-dogs">Guide/assistance dogs  </h3>
<p>City Hall welcomes all guide and assistance dogs, as well as other assistance animals. Please note that no other dogs or pets are permitted. Upon arrival, please advise the security officer of the assistance dog, security officers are briefed on the admission policy.  </p>
<h3 id="fire-safety">Fire safety  </h3>
<p>In the case of an evacuation, a voice alarm will direct people to leave by the nearest fire exit. We have no visual alarm system at City Hall. Our security officers will check all areas and guide visitors out of the building during an evacuation. </p>
  </div>

      </div>

<h2 id="accessible-visitor-parking-152536-title" class="h2">
                                          Accessible visitor parking
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>There are two parking bays available for blue badge holders. These are accessed via Kamal Chunchie Way, past the security gate, next to the cycle parking.  The parking bays are approximately 80m from the entrance. Please note that parking cannot be guaranteed. </p>
<p>The security team will be aware of the vehicle at the barrier. Upon arrival at the barriers, the driver will to speak with City Hall security officers by using an intercom, dialling 020 7055 6700 or speaking with a security officer in person to gain entry.</p>
<p>If you have an appointment to see a member of staff at City Hall and require use of a blue badge parking bay, please ask them to enquire about the availability of parking spaces.</p>
<p>Please contact <a href="mailto:reception@london.gov.uk">reception@london.gov.uk</a> in advance to reserve a space.  </p>

  </div>

<h2 id="accessible-toilets-152538-title" class="h2">
                                          Accessible toilets
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>All toilet facilities in City Hall are gender neutral. Accessible toilet cubicles are located on the ground floor, one next to the cafe and Chamber. The other two are located near the Committee Rooms. One cubicle has a sliding door.</p>

  </div>

<h2 id="changing-places-152540-title" class="h2">
                                          Changing Places
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>City Hall has worked with Changing Places to install an accessible toilet and changing facility. It located next to the reception desk on the ground floor. </p>
<ul>
<li>a height-adjustable, adult-sized changing bench with shower</li>
<li>a ceiling track hoist system </li>
<li>adequate space in the changing area for a wheelchair user and up to two assistants </li>
<li>a centrally placed toilet with space either side for assistants </li>
<li>wide tear-off paper roll to cover the bench </li>
<li>a large waste bin for disposable pads </li>
<li>a non-slip floor.</li>
</ul>
<p>For more information, please visit the <a href="https://www.changing-places.org/">Changing Places website</a>.</p>

  </div>

<h2 id="hearing-and-induction-loop-152542-title" class="h2">
                                          Hearing and induction loop
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>Public areas of City Hall including the reception desk, Chamber, Committee Rooms and the London’s Living Room have an inbuilt induction loop. The induction loops are always on, users may need to switch their device to the ‘T-setting’.</p>
<h3 id="convo">Convo</h3>
<p>We’ve partnered with <a href="https://uk.convo.io/UserWebApp">Convo, a deaf-led interpreting service</a>, to make it easy to reach a BSL Interpreter.</p>
<p>If you use BSL, you can call us through the Convo Now app on iOS, Android, or a web browser. Simply find us in the Community Directory. When you connect, the interpreter will check who you’d like to speak with and support the conversation.</p>
<p>Alternatively, with Convo Access, find the green Convo QR codes at the reception desk, scan the QR code and connect to a qualified remote BSL interpreter for in person face to face communication.</p>
  </div>

<h2 id="mental-health-wellbeing-and-neurodiversity-152544-title" class="h2">
                                          Mental health, wellbeing and neurodiversity
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>Our surroundings will affect people in different ways, we want to ensure that all visitors to City Hall feel as comfortable as possible. The following are in place which may support the needs of people who experience mental health distress or who are neurodiverse.  </p>
<p>Large glass panels provide natural light inside the building and a sense of open space. There are benches and seating located in the public areas, where visitors can seek quieter spaces if needed. Gardens surrounding the building provide a quiet space to relax, with views over the Royal Docks.</p>
<p>City Hall is a lively workplace, quieter spaces may vary depending on events taking place, please speak with reception or a security officer for advice on finding a quieter space on the day of your visit or contact us in advance of your visit.</p>

  </div>

<h2 id="dementia-friends-152546-title" class="h2">
                                          Dementia Friends
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>City Hall is a certified Dementia Friendly Venue. Many of our front of house staff, including reception and security officers, are trained as Dementia Friends. These staff can be identified by a small flower pin badge. </p>
<p>All public areas are visible from the entrance. There is clear signage directing visitors to meeting rooms and facilities.  </p>

<div class="rich-text">
      <p>Seating is available in the reception area, the café and the London’s Living Room.  </p>
<p>The Chamber has six dedicated spaces for wheelchair users in the public gallery. </p>

<div class="rich-text">
      <p>If you have any questions about your visit to City Hall, or if you would like us to make adjustments or changes to enable your visit, please email <a href="mailto:reception@london.gov.uk">reception@london.gov.uk</a> or call 020 7983 4000.</p>
<p>Responses to postal enquiries will take a little longer, our contact address is: </p>
<p>FAO GLA E16,                     <br>
C/O Xerox Unit 4,                                             <br>
191 Pasadena Close,                                      <br>
Hayes,<br>
UB3 3NQ.</p>
<p>We are always looking to improve visitor experience, we welcome feedback and comments regarding your visit to City Hall either on the day by speaking to reception or security officers, or by email <a href="mailto:reception@london.gov.uk">reception@london.gov.uk</a> after your visit.   </p>

<h2 id="context-147013-title" class="h2">
                    1. Context
            </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>The Festival of Ideas (FOI) events created a space for communities to explore:</p>

<ul>
	<li>what strong communities look like</li>
	<li>where they come together</li>
	<li>what’s needed for recovery from the pandemic</li>
</ul>

<p>79 event organisers gave feedback about what they learnt.</p>

<p>Event organisers and stakeholders contributed to the analysis of this feedback. The process was facilitated by a research consultant.</p>

<p>The learning is being used to inform the design and development of the ‘building stronger communities’ mission as part of the GLA London Recovery Programme.</p>

<p> </p>

<p> </p>

  </div>

      </div>

<h2 id="participatory-workshops-147015-title" class="h2">
                    2. Participatory workshops
            </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>Two workshops were attended by representatives of more than 20 community groups, charities and civil society organisations involved in the Festival of Ideas.</p>

<p>In workshop 1 (October 4th 2021), participants</p>

<ul>
	<li>Learnt about the insights emerging from the GLA festival of ideas</li>
	<li>Contributed to the analysis of the feedback gathered from events</li>
	<li>Identified key insights and discussed what makes a stronger community.</li>
</ul>

<p>In workshop 2 (October 18th 2021), participants</p>

<ul>
	<li>Reviewed a synthesis of the findings as to what makes a stronger community</li>
	<li>Learnt more about and highlighted how they could contribute to the GLA’s shared action plan </li>
	<li>Discussed what they needed to contribute further and how to continue the relationship</li>
</ul>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>


          










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-py-8 lg:u-py-9 xl:u-py-12 xxl:u-py-14 u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h2 id="stronger-community-themes-147017-title" class="h2">
                    3. Stronger community themes
            </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>The themes define how communities, organisations and the GLA can actively collaborate to actively cultivate a stronger community. </p>

<p>They are based on:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Independent thematic analysis of feedback</li>
	<li>Collective analysis and discussion with event organisers to interpret the analysis</li>
	<li>Cross referencing with recent research to measure the strength of communities</li>
</ul>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>


          










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-py-8 lg:u-py-9 xl:u-py-12 xxl:u-py-14 u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h2 id="what-are-strong-communities-147061-title" class="h2">
                    4. What are strong communities?
            </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>Together, we have identified 7 key elements of strong communities.</p>

<ol>
	<li>Services meet local needs</li>
	<li>Opportunities to come together </li>
	<li>Places and spaces for the community</li>
	<li>Voice and ownership </li>
	<li>Commitment to diversity and inclusion </li>
	<li>Safety</li>
	<li>Funding and support </li>
</ol>

  </div>

      </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h3 id="services-meet-local-needs-147026-title" class="h3">
                    4.1 Services meet local needs
            </h3>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>A strong community is one in which services are accessible, equitable, responsive and representative of diverse and changing community needs. They are trusted by the community.<br>
 </p>

  </div>

      </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="access-to-services-detail-147020-title" class="h4">
                    4.1.1 Access to services: Detail
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <ul>
	<li>Includes <strong>public services</strong> (council services, education, housing, health, and social care) and services provided by <strong>charity and community groups</strong>. </li>
	<li>There should be services to meet <strong>essential needs</strong> and <strong>build community</strong>.</li>
	<li>Services needed are not the same everywhere, there is <strong>no ‘one size fits all</strong>’.</li>
	<li>Services are fundamental to supporting communities to thrive when they: 
	<ul>
		<li>Provide essential and accessible support</li>
		<li>Respond to specific local needs</li>
		<li>Relevant to community needs identified by communities themselves</li>
		<li>Tackle structural inequalities</li>
		<li>Support the making of community</li>
		<li>Have the trust of the community</li>
		<li>Are designed and delivered by and with the communities they are for.</li>
	</ul>
	</li>
</ul>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="festival-of-ideas-event-organiser-feedback-what-did-you-learn-about-how-londoners-imagine-strong-communities-147022-title" class="h4">
                    4.1.2 Festival of Ideas event organiser feedback: “What did you learn about how Londoners imagine strong communities?”
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>"[A strong community] should mean living as long and as healthily as everyone in the country. It should mean full employment and social justice for all, with <strong>key and essential services</strong>, provided not-for-profit. Many times grassroots organisations have the <strong>trust</strong> of the community. There should be adequate hubs for <strong>ALL residents</strong> to share the growing regenerated changes happening throughout our boroughs."</p>

<p><br>
 </p>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="festival-of-ideas-event-organiser-feedback-what-did-you-learn-about-how-londoners-imagine-strong-communities-147024-title" class="h4">
                    4.1.3 Festival of Ideas event organiser feedback: “What did you learn about how Londoners imagine strong communities?”
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>"Too often, the volunteers and the wide range of service users we work with have felt that they are sought for consultation, but not deemed <strong>good enough to create solutions for the challenges faced</strong> by the whole community."</p>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h3 id="opportunities-to-come-together-147032-title" class="h3">
                    4.2 Opportunities to come together
            </h3>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>A strong community has opportunities to come together and connect with others based on a shared interest, identity, experience or activity. Communities actively support one another.</p>

  </div>

      </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="opportunities-to-come-together-detail-147028-title" class="h4">
                    4.2.1 Opportunities to come together: Detail
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <ul>
	<li>Social activities form the basis for social connections and future supportive relationships.</li>
	<li>Formal or social events and activities build a sense of belonging or offer mutual support.</li>
	<li>The community should play an active role in defining and delivering opportunities.</li>
	<li>Creative, artistic, music, physical activities, entertainment and food often to draw people in, especially if they are free. They give a sense of purpose and reason to come together.</li>
	<li>Voluntary and community organisations playing a key role in creating opportunities to come together, as well as supporting people to access these opportunities.</li>
	<li>Some communities have a shared identity, but need funding, space and purpose to come together again. Others need impetus to come together and forge a sense of community.</li>
</ul>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="festival-of-ideas-event-organiser-feedback-what-did-you-learn-about-how-londoners-imagine-strong-communities-147030-title" class="h4">
                    4.2.2 Festival of Ideas event organiser feedback: “What did you learn about how Londoners imagine strong communities?”
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>“<strong>Coming together is valuable</strong> for communities. It helps <strong>make sure people belong</strong>, have a good life, have fun, are safe. It doesn't happen enough and is really important after the pandemic. </p>

<p><strong>However, communities are not mixing naturally</strong> - they need to be pushed to make this happen. This is even more important post-COVID - we need to keep working together.”</p>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h3 id="places-and-spaces-for-the-community-147038-title" class="h3">
                    4.3 Places and spaces for the community
            </h3>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p><br>
Stronger communities have places and spaces that enable communities to come together, participate in community activities and access services.</p>

  </div>

      </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="places-and-spaces-detail-147034-title" class="h4">
                    4.3.1 Places and spaces: Detail
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <ul>
	<li>Places and spaces <strong>for the community to come together</strong> include <strong>a range of buildings, online spaces</strong>, high streets, parks, transport hubs, schools and others <strong>venues</strong> offering space for non profit, public and commercial use.</li>
	<li>Community venues do not necessarily need to be dedicated buildings or fixed locations (as long as there are spaces available regularly).</li>
	<li>Community spaces enable people to come together, access services and participate in community activities. They become <strong>focal points</strong> for a <strong>range </strong>of communities.</li>
	<li>They can also be <strong>online</strong>, although there is a <strong>strong desire to reconnect in physical locations</strong> following the social isolation of lockdown during the COVID-19 pandemic.</li>
	<li>Community spaces should be <strong>free</strong> (or funded), <strong>safe, accessible and inclusive</strong>. They feel relevant and in-keeping as a focal point for the community to come together.</li>
	<li><strong>People coming together socially </strong>define and build a community place / space. </li>
</ul>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="festival-of-ideas-event-organiser-feedback-what-did-you-learn-about-how-londoners-imagine-strong-communities-147036-title" class="h4">
                    4.3.2 Festival of Ideas event organiser feedback: “What did you learn about how Londoners imagine strong communities?”
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>“Community is<strong> more than just a building</strong>. Buildings may be an important feature of the community, but the community is made by people. Whilst prayer services may be what often brings our communities together, it is the baby groups and other <strong>social activities which make the community</strong>. Strong communities are about strong relationships, with everyone feeling like they have a part to play.”</p>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h3 id="voice-and-ownership-147044-title" class="h3">
                    4.4 Voice and ownership
            </h3>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>Strong communities have voice and ownership, taking responsibility for building their community, actively express their views and shaping the future of their communities.</p>

  </div>

      </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="voice-and-ownership-detail-147040-title" class="h4">
                    4.4.1 Voice and ownership: Detail
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <ul>
	<li>Communities <strong>actively participate</strong> in building the community they want to be part of, mobilising around a shared purpose and coming together to achieve this. </li>
	<li>Communities also take <strong>ownership and responsibility</strong> to improve the future of their community, acting to influence change in community activities, services or policy.</li>
	<li>A <strong>wider sense of inclusion, belonging and safety</strong> is vital to community members and groups feeling able to express their views, to be heard and influence change. </li>
	<li>A lack of <strong>trust in public institutions and/or community organisations</strong>, structural inequalities and a history of being consulted (without evidence of being heard) are barriers to a strong community with voice and ownership to influence change. </li>
	<li><strong>Bringing people together across different communities</strong> (not just in silo’s) helps create a sense of shared vision (and a broader community identity) and a collective voice. </li>
	<li>Crucial to recognise that everyone has strengths and brings valuable perspectives. </li>
</ul>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="festival-of-ideas-event-organiser-feedback-what-did-you-learn-about-how-londoners-imagine-strong-communities-147042-title" class="h4">
                    4.4.2 Festival of Ideas event organiser feedback: “What did you learn about how Londoners imagine strong communities?”
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>“Communities <strong>come together with a shared vision and goal:</strong> to make the world a more enjoyable place- between people and for the environment. <strong>Giving people a voice</strong>, creates better environments for people to then <strong>develop closer relationships with each other.</strong> Breaking bread together (we had food and drink) enables those conversations to begin.”</p>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h3 id="commitment-to-diversity-and-inclusion-147050-title" class="h3">
                    4.5 Commitment to diversity and inclusion
            </h3>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>Strong communities have a commitment to diversity and inclusion ensuring that efforts to build communities address community cohesion, inclusion, accessibility and structural inequalities.</p>

  </div>

      </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="diversity-and-inclusion-detail-147046-title" class="h4">
                    4.5.1 Diversity and inclusion: Detail
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <ul>
	<li>Communities <strong>largely come together around shared identities,</strong> backgrounds, experiences, locations and interests to create a shared sense of <strong>belonging</strong>.</li>
	<li>London is an aspirational community of shared identity, where diverse communities are recognised and celebrated.</li>
	<li>There is <strong>a risk of communities coming together in siloes</strong>. It is vital that there are varied opportunities to bring people together across different communities.</li>
	<li>Efforts to bring communities together <strong>need to focus explicitly on equality, diversity and inclusion</strong>. This will be beyond the remit of a single event or community and this should be explored collectively.</li>
	<li>Bringing different communities together <strong>can be hard and fraught with tension</strong>. It takes <strong>people dedicated</strong> to making this happen (along with money, resources, support).</li>
</ul>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="festival-of-ideas-event-organiser-feedback-what-did-you-learn-about-how-londoners-imagine-strong-communities-147048-title" class="h4">
                    4.5.2 Festival of Ideas event organiser feedback: “What did you learn about how Londoners imagine strong communities?”
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>“Like a garden where different flowers of different colours and smells <strong>grow side by side</strong> and together increase beauty of the garden. There will be no discrimination, no racism, no misunderstanding, no difference between black and white, poor and rich, <strong>people of different communities</strong> live together peacefully and participate in building the community stronger. Communities <strong>come together through activities</strong>.”</p>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h3 id="6-safety-147056-title" class="h3">
                    4.6 6. Safety
            </h3>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>Strong communities feel safe for those who live there, including safe from crime, persecution, racism and abuse. Communities are inclusive and community members feel safe expressing their views and identities.</p>

  </div>

      </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="safety-detail-147052-title" class="h4">
                    4.6.1 Safety: Detail
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <ul>
	<li>People feel safe when they are<strong> secure and happy where they live</strong>.</li>
	<li>Strong communities <strong>are safe and feel safe</strong> for those who live there, including safe from <strong>crime, persecution, racism and abuse</strong>.</li>
	<li>When communities lack <strong>trust in the police and criminal justice system</strong>, they do not feel safe to come together, are more likely to exist in isolation or in conflict.</li>
	<li>People also need to <strong>feel safe expressing their views, having a voice</strong> and know that they will be listened to or heard.</li>
	<li>Key <strong>challenges</strong> include inequality, racism, discrimination, a lack of trust of public services.</li>
	<li>Safety is <strong>interwoven with a sense of belonging</strong> to a community. However, diversity thinking needs to underpin this. Some communities are less inclusive of different identities.</li>
	<li>A lack of trust, understanding and <strong>connections between communities</strong> can undermine safety.</li>
</ul>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="festival-of-ideas-event-organiser-feedback-what-did-you-learn-about-how-londoners-imagine-strong-communities-147054-title" class="h4">
                    4.6.2 Festival of Ideas event organiser feedback: “What did you learn about how Londoners imagine strong communities?”
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>"We are <strong>able to exist</strong> in a space where there is no need to explain our identities."</p>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h3 id="funding-and-support-147060-title" class="h3">
                    4.7 Funding and support
            </h3>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>Strong communities have funding and support for people, community groups and organisations to lead initiatives and come together, with access to support that helps strengthen their efforts.</p>

  </div>

      </div>

    










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h4 id="funding-and-support-detail-147058-title" class="h4">
                    4.7.1 Funding and support: Detail
            </h4>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <ul>
	<li>Resources and funding <strong>enable</strong> communities to come together and support one another. </li>
	<li><strong>Costs</strong> include venue hire, food, publicity, event administration, insurance and support. </li>
	<li><strong>Access to spaces, places or venues</strong> that are accessible, affordable, inclusive and enable communities to come together is a specific challenge faced by many communities. </li>
	<li>Organisations need longer term or regular funding to come together (beyond one off events) in order to focus on building stronger communities.</li>
	<li><strong>Some spaces and assets locally are underutilised</strong>, (e.g. schools after school hours).</li>
	<li>It is important <strong>funding</strong> is given by <strong>trusted</strong> organisations, <strong>underpinned by equality, accessibility and community needs</strong>. This should<strong> recognise expertise in communities</strong> and ideally share power for decision making with communities.</li>
</ul>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>


          










  
<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-py-8 lg:u-py-9 xl:u-py-12 xxl:u-py-14 u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h2 id="the-london-civic-strength-index-147063-title" class="h2">
                    5. The London Civic Strength Index
            </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10 section-field-container">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>The London Civic Strength Index helps London boroughs and organisations support discussions about the strengths of their communities and consider how build on them.</p>

<p>It was developed by the Young Foundation with funding by the GLA and informed by the views of Londoners captured during the Festival of Ideas.</p>

<p>The themes identified here align with the index.</p>

<p> </p>

      <div class="rich-text">
<p><strong>What is it?</strong></p>
<p>The <a href="/rogue-landlord-checker">Rogue Landlord and Agent Checker</a> is a new public database introduced by Mayor Sadiq Khan. It names and shames unscrupulous private landlords and letting agents who have been prosecuted or fined for housing offences such as allowing homes to fall into a bad or dangerous condition - for example, through overcrowding, providing poor escape routes or badly maintained fire doors.</p>
<p><strong>How does it work?</strong></p>
<p>The checker allows you to find out whether a current or future landlord has a record of such offences, to help you make an informed choice about where you live. It will also allow you to easily report a landlord or agent whom you suspect of unscrupulous practices.</p>
<p><strong>Who does the checker cover?</strong></p>
<p>At the moment, landlords and agents from ten boroughs - Brent, Camden, Greenwich, Islington, Kingston, Newham, Southwark, Sutton, Waltham Forest and Westminster - are on the database. This will allow 600,000 tenants, a quarter of London renters, to check for rogue landlords and agents in their area.</p>
<p><strong>What about other boroughs?</strong></p>
<p>Eight more boroughs - Barking and Dagenham, Croydon, Enfield, Hackney, Haringey, Lewisham, Redbridge and Tower Hamlets - will submit records to the database in the next few weeks. The Mayor wants all London councils to add their data, to help protect tenants in their areas.</p>
<p><strong>What information is on there?</strong></p>
<p>You can use the checker to see:</p>
<p>o        Landlords and agents’ full names</p>
<p>o        What type of action was taken against them, for what offence, and any fines</p>
<p>o        Who undertook the enforcement - for example, a London borough</p>
<p>o        The address of the property where the offence took place</p>
<p>o        Part of the landlord’s home address</p>
<p>For legal reasons, names are only visible to the public for a limited time, typically 12 months. A private database will hold records for up to 10 years, to allow authorities to get a full picture of a landlord or agent’s past when conducting investigations.</p>
<p><strong>Where can I find it?</strong></p>
<p>The Rogue Landlord and Agent Checker is on the City Hall website here: <a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/rogue-landlord-checker">www.london.gov.uk/rogue-landlord-checker</a></p>

<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<p><em>Simon Powell, Assistant Director - Strategic Projects and Propert, explains why releasing empty land will benefit Londoners…</em></p>
<p>Back in April 2012, we inherited 635 hectares of land and became one of the largest public sector landowners in London. The Mayor pledged to release all the unused land for development. This would encourage investment, create jobs and provide much needed homes for Londoners.</p>
<p>All of the developable land now has now been released. This means nearly 50,000 homes will be built across the sites and almost 60,000 jobs created in new workspaces. There will also be new schools, bridges, parks, health centres and community facilities.</p>
<p>The sites include London’s Royal Docks, which will host the capital’s next business district and become a hub for emerging technologies. There’s also Greenwich Peninsula, the largest single regeneration development in London.</p>
<p><a href="/programmes-strategies/housing-and-land/land-and-development">Find out more</a>.</p>
<p><a data-flickr-embed="true" href="https://www.flickr.com/photos/greaterlondonauthority/24167965579/in/dateposted/" title="Beam Park Land Legacy"><img src="https://farm2.staticflickr.com/1512/24167965579_b3e2a5ab62_z.jpg" width="453" height="640" alt="Beam Park Land Legacy"></a></p>

<h2 id="in-this-section-71784-title" class="h2">
                                          In this section
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<h4 id="by-karen-lawrence-commissioner-on-the-london-sustainable-development-commission"><a href="/who-we-are/city-halls-partners/london-sustainable-development-commission/who-we-are/meet-commissioners#acc-i-53102">By Karen Lawrence, Commissioner on the London Sustainable Development Commission</a></h4>
<p>I have the privilege of leading an exciting project for the London Sustainable Development Commission (LSDC) that’s all about getting more women into and leading the city’s cleantech industry. This is the sector that produces the technologies, goods and services that reduce negative impacts on our environment, and it’s an important and growing part of London’s economy.</p>
<p>The LSDC’s <a href="/who-we-are/city-halls-partners/london-sustainable-development-commission/our-current-work-and-priorities/our-cleantech-and-innovation-work/our-women-cleantech-work">Women in Cleantech project</a> is taking place at an auspicious time. Throughout 2018, to mark the centenary of the first women winning the right to vote in the UK, the Mayor of London’s <a href="/who-we-are/what-mayor-does/behindeverygreatcity" target="_blank">#BehindEveryGreatCity</a> campaign is celebrating the city’s role in the women’s suffrage movement. This will mark the progress that’s been made for and by women over the past 100 years, and take real action to tackle gender inequality in London. As part of this, I had the great privilege to attend the unveiling of the statue of suffragist Millicent Fawcett earlier this year – the first statue of a woman by a woman in Parliament Square. The Mayor is also rolling out Better Futures, a project designed to give 100 small cleantech businesses the boost they need to be successful, and create a hub for low-carbon industries in London.</p>
<p>Over the last couple of months, we’ve surveyed and met with some great women contributors from the field during our research and workshops. This has given us some fantastic insight into what prevents women entering the cleantech sector and/or staying there to realise their true potential. On Wednesday 13 June, we hosted a solutions workshop in City Hall to look at these issues in more detail, and start working on what we’ll do about them, so the cleantech sector can benefit from what these amazing women have to offer.</p>
<p>We’re grateful to Shirley Rodrigues (Deputy Mayor for Environment and Energy) for setting out London’s ambitions for the sector and how this project can help inform them. We’re also grateful to Juliet Davenport (CEO & Founder, Good Energy), Dr. Hayaatun Sillem (CEO, Royal Academy of Engineering) and Louise Wilson (CEO, Abundance Investment), who kicked us off with some personal insights into their experiences in the sector.</p>
<p>There was consensus that students are made to choose too early in their lives between the sciences and the arts – a complete contradiction to working life where businesses need communicators who understand science, and scientists or mathematicians with effective communication skills. We learned that we can all do more by sharing our own career stories, such as in schools or via social media. And we learned the importance of male role models who treat women as equals in the workplace; these can be just as important as female ones.</p>
<p>As we passed the microphone to over 60 talented and enthusiastic women (and some equally talented men as well), the energy in the room was electric! Many issues raised were not unique to the cleantech sector: unconscious gender bias, ‘imposter syndrome’ and relatively low female participation in STEM subjects all emerged. But some sector-specific topics were also raised. This included a sense that the cleantech sector was one in which it was possible to have a social purpose and deliver global impact in equal measure – something that was likely to attract women into the industry and so should be promoted.</p>
<p>But this project isn’t about initiating ‘special measures’ for women because we’re needy! Indeed, studies show that businesses with women at strategic and senior management levels generally outperform businesses with no, or fewer, women in these positions. This is about a basic understanding that to build the best of anything you need a wide range of tools in your toolbox. It reminds me of the old proverb “If all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail”. To be the best leader, male or female, you need to be able to get the best out of everyone in your team. Time to put more of those leadership tools, personal and institutional, into the cleantech toolbox!</p>
<p>Our next step is to use what we’ve heard to facilitate discussions with the cleantech community about which support programmes we think should be developed or strengthened to help more women enter this sector. Watch out for our report which will be published on our website later this year.</p>
<p>We’re keen to hear what individuals and organisations making up the cleantech ecosystem can do to help increase the number of women entering and leading the cleantech sector.  If you’re interested in knowing more or in getting involved, please <a href="mailto:LSDC@london.gov.uk?subject=Women%20in%20Cleantech%3A%20please%20tell%20me%20more">contact us</a>.</p>
</div>

<div class="rich-text">
      <p>Karen Lawrence has spent the past 30 years in several diverse sectors and a mixture of blue chip and SME organisations. Working for the Energy Saving Trust for over 10 years provided Karen with a robust platform of broader sustainability knowledge and specifically on working with communities on sustainability. This was further strengthened in a role as a trustee and latterly Vice Chair of Pure Leapfrog. For the LSDC, Karen is currently leading on a key project to identify and address barriers to inclusivity in the cleantech sector.</p>

<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<p>Sarah B, Senior Events Officer at City Hall, explains why you should come and explore your city, join in fun outdoor activities and put a spring in your step at our new festival this Spring....</p>
<p>From 18-28 March, we’re inviting you to celebrate London’s great outdoor spaces from gardens to parks, high streets to marketplaces. The 11-day Find Your London festival features over 100 events in each and every corner of London.  That means it’s a brilliant opportunity to discover new places. Or simply enter your postcode to find out what’s happening near you using our special map.</p>
<p>There’ll be everything from yoga in the park, cycle trails and treasure hunts, to beekeeping, an Alice in Wonderland Tea Party and much more besides. In fact, there’s something to suit every mood. There are also activities for every age, from eight to 80 and lots for families to enjoy too. As with all the best things in life, many of the events are free.</p>
<p>If all this sounds a little overwhelming, help is at hand. So you can make your mind up and make the most of the festival, we’ve come up with five different moods. So whether you’re looking to be Active, Curious, Playful, Relaxed, or Inspired you’ll find a great day out at Find Your London.</p>
<p><a href="http://london.gov.uk/findyourlondon">Find out more</a><strong> #findyourLDN</strong></p>

  <div class="u-py-8 lg:u-py-9 xl:u-py-12 xxl:u-py-14">

<h2 id="in-this-section-28845-title" class="h2">
                                          In this section
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<p>RE:NEW provides a highly skilled and experienced Support Team offering free support to social landlords, local authorities and private landlords to help get home energy retrofit projects and programmes up and running across Greater London.</p>
<p><a href="https://gallery.mailchimp.com/f10560436fe081703bde39e6a/files/RENEW_EXPERT_TEAM.01.pdf">Read more about the RE:NEW Support Team</a></p>
<p>RE:NEW support is tailored to each organisation and can comprise of a review of retrofit potential, formulation of retrofit projects, funding and procurement advice and support through the procurement process.</p>
</div>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-py-8 lg:u-py-9 xl:u-py-12 xxl:u-py-14 u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h2 id="support-services-28847-title" class="h2">
                                          Support services
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<p>The areas of support provided by the team include:</p>
<div class="scrollable-table u-overflow-auto custom-scrollbar" x-on:scroll.throttle="onScroll" x-data="scrollableTable" :class="classes" x-on:resize.window.debounce="init">
<table border="1" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="1" style="width: 500px;">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="width: 200px;"><strong>CROHM stock assessment                     </strong></td>
<td>RE:NEW offers a market leading stock assessment service – <a href="http://www.parityprojects.com/professionals/crohm-retrofit-stock-assessment/">Carbon Reduction Options for Housing Managers (CROHM)</a>. CROHM helps design and implement strategic retrofit programmes by making use of your housing data and ensuring that the analysis accurately reflects the retrofit potential of your stock.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Programme optimisation</strong></td>
<td>Programme optimisation is linked strongly to a stock assessment and funding and finance support. It is designed to ensure the best return on investment from existing and planned programmes and ensure all opportunities to increase energy savings are explored.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>The business case for retrofit</strong></td>
<td>The Support Team can provide in-depth data analytics services to help identify where robust savings from wider housing cost areas (for example, reduced repairs and maintenance, customer contacts, rent arrears and voids) can be realised. <a href="/sites/default/files/renew_business_case_flyer_-_february_2017.pdf">Read more</a>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Funding and finance support</strong></td>
<td>
<p>RE:NEW will help organisations to identify and secure the right mix of funding and finance for retrofit programmes.The RE:NEW Funding Guide also summarises the latest funding and financing available for retrofit. RE:NEW is working closely with ECO suppliers and has Memoranda of Understanding with British Gas, EDF, EON, NPower, SSE and Scottish Power.</p>
<p><a href="/sites/default/files/re_new_funding_guide.pdf">Read more</a>.</p>
</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Technical risks</strong></td>
<td>Protecting retrofit projects from technical risk and unintended outcomes is vital to achieving a return on investment and maintaining confidence in retrofit. RE:NEW's review of energy performance related risks includes thermal bridging, ventilation and any associated potential for damp, mould, condensation or energy performance issues. The RE:NEW service does not cover, certify or in any way replace the need for appropriate measures to address health and safety, structural integrity, electrical or other risks that are subject to regulatory compliance. Read <a href="/sites/default/files/technical_risk_june_2017.pdf">RE:NEW's technical risk flyer</a>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Low carbon technology</strong></td>
<td>RE:NEW can provide support with implementing low carbon technologies, identifying the potential for communal heating systems and installation of solar PV. Read <a href="/sites/default/files/communal_heating_flyer.pdf">RE:NEW's communal heating flyer</a>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Planning support</strong></td>
<td>Planning requirements are recognised to be a significant obstacle to retrofit, particularly in traditional buildings. The RE:NEW Support Team eases engagement with planning authorities and helps develop an understanding of planning requirements and how they affect the technical aspects of retrofit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Marketing and engagement advice</strong>  </td>
<td>RE:NEW offers specialist marketing and communication services to help your retrofit schemes and projects achieve maximum uptake. <a href="/sites/default/files/gla_migrate_files_destination/140409%20GLA_Marketing_And_Communications_v2.pdf">Read more</a>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Procurement support</strong></td>
<td>RE:NEW will support you through the retrofit procurement process, from providing procurement options, through to strategy development and specification review, to tender assessment and moderation. Read more about our <a href="/sites/default/files/gla_migrate_files_destination/GLA_Procurement%20framework%20V3.pdf">procurement framework and support</a> and read <a href="/sites/default/files/cp00052_procurement_blogv1.pdf">RE:NEW's blog on tips for a successful procurement process</a>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
<p>The RE:NEW Support Team can support projects involving all types of efficiency measures. Typical measures include:</p>
<ul>
<li>loft and cavity wall insulation</li>
<li>solid wall insulation</li>
<li>heating improvements</li>
<li>water saving measures</li>
<li>double or triple glazing</li>
<li>draught proofing</li>
<li>district heating</li>
<li>renewable energy generation</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="in-this-section-59863-title" class="h2">

      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<p><meta charset="utf-8"></p>
<p>This accessibility statement applies to <a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/who-we-are/what-london-assembly-does/questions-mayor/find-an-answer">london.gov.uk/who-we-are/what-london-assembly-does/questions-mayor/find-an-answer</a></p>
<p>The Mayor’s Question Time site is run by the Greater London Authority (GLA).</p>
<p>We want as many people as possible to be able to use these websites. For example, that means you should be able to:</p>
<ul>
<li>change colours, contrast levels and fonts</li>
<li>zoom in up to 400% without the text spilling off the screen</li>
<li>navigate most of the website using just a keyboard</li>
<li>navigate most of the website using speech recognition software</li>
<li>listen to most of the website using a screen reader (including the most recent versions of JAWS, NVDA and VoiceOver)</li>
</ul>
<p>We’ve also made the website text as simple as possible to understand.</p>
<p><a href="https://mcmw.abilitynet.org.uk/">AbilityNet</a> has advice on making your device easier to use if you have a disability.</p>
</div>

<h2 id="how-accessible-is-this-website-59865-title" class="h2">

      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<p>This site has been built to be as accessible as possible and tested against WCAG 2.2 AA. There are some areas which are not yet fully accessible:</p>
<ul>
<li>Some data tables do not correctly identify column and row heading cells</li>
</ul>

                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <p>If you find any problems not listed on this page or think we’re not meeting accessibility requirements, contact our Public Liaison Unit via the details below.</p>
<p>If you need information on this website in a different format like accessible PDF, large print, easy read, audio recording or braille:</p>
<ul>
<li>call 020 7983 4000 (Monday to Friday, 9am - 5pm)</li>
<li><a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/contact-us-form">get in touch via our online form</a></li>
<li>email <a href="mailto:mayor@london.gov.uk">mayor@london.gov.uk</a> </li>
</ul>
<p>We will consider your request and get back to you within five working days, to advise further.</p>
<p>If you cannot view the map on our <a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/who-we-are/city-halls-buildings-and-squares/how-find-city-hall">contact us page</a>, please call or email us for directions.</p>

<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<p class="BodyTextSpaced" style="margin-bottom:8px">The Greater London Authority is committed to making its website accessible, in accordance with the Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) (No. 2) Accessibility Regulations 2018.</p>
<h3 style="margin-top:16px; margin-bottom:8px" id="compliance-status">Compliance status</h3>
<p class="BodyTextSpaced" style="margin-bottom:8px">This website is partially compliant with the <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/" rel="external">Web Content Accessibility Guidelines version 2.2</a> AA standard, due to the non-compliances listed below.</p>

<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<p>The content listed below is non-accessible for the following reasons.</p>
<h3 id="non-compliance-with-the-accessibility-regulations">Non compliance with the accessibility regulations</h3>
<ul>
<li>Some data tables do not correctly identify column and row heading cells (WCAG 2.2 A criterion 1.3.1 - Info and relationships)</li>
</ul>
<p>We plan to investigate and fix the listed issues by December 2025.</p>
<h3 id="disproportionate-burden">Disproportionate burden</h3>
<p>Disproportionate burden does not apply to any of the non-compliances listed in the accessibility statement.</p>

  "headLine": "Apply to the EU Settlement Scheme (settled and pre-settled status)",
  "description": "The EU Settlement Scheme for EU citizens and their families to remain in the UK after it leaves the EU ('Brexit'): who's eligible, how to apply, how much it costs. ",
  "articleBody": "\u003cp\u003eYou can apply using any device, for example, a laptop, Android device or iPhone.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ca href=\"/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/what-youll-need-to-apply\"\u003eCheck what you’ll need\u003c/a\u003e before you apply.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eIf you have pre-settled status already, it will be extended by 5 years before it’s due to expire. You’ll be sent an email telling you when this happens.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eIf you’re eligible, your extended pre-settled status may be automatically converted to settled status or you can apply for settled status. \u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eFind out more about \u003ca href=\"/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/switch-from-presettled-status-to-settled-status\"\u003emoving from pre-settled status to settled status\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003ch2 id=\"apply\"\u003eApply\u003c/h2\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eThe deadline for applying for most people was 30 June 2021. You can still apply if either:\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethe deadline for you to apply is after 30 June 2021\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eyou have \u003ca href=\"/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/eligibility\"\u003e‘reasonable grounds’ for why you’re applying now, and not by the deadline or in the time since the deadline passed\u003c/a\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eIf you’re \u003ca href=\"/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/apply-settled-status-for-child\"\u003eapplying for yourself and your children\u003c/a\u003e, make your own application first.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ca class=\"gem-c-button govuk-button govuk-button--start\" role=\"button\" data-module=\"govuk-button\" data-ga4-attributes='{\"event_name\":\"navigation\",\"type\":\"start button\"}' draggable=\"false\" href=\"https://apply-to-visit-or-stay-in-the-uk.homeoffice.gov.uk/euss\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Start now \u003c/span\u003e\u003csvg class=\"govuk-button__start-icon govuk-!-display-none-print\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"17.5\" height=\"19\" viewbox=\"0 0 33 40\" focusable=\"false\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath fill=\"currentColor\" d=\"M0 0h13l20 20-20 20H0l20-20z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eThe Home Office will use the personal information you provide to decide whether to grant your application. Find out \u003ca href=\"/guidance/eu-settlement-scheme-how-we-use-your-personal-information\"\u003ehow the Home Office will process your personal information\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003ch2 id=\"continue-your-application\"\u003eContinue your application\u003c/h2\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eIf you’ve already started to apply, you can \u003ca rel=\"external\" href=\"https://apply-to-visit-or-stay-in-the-uk.homeoffice.gov.uk/dashboard/\"\u003econtinue your application\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003ch2 id=\"who-cannot-use-this-service\"\u003eWho cannot use this service\u003c/h2\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eYou cannot use the online service to apply to the scheme if you’re applying as:\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethe family member of a British citizen you lived with in the \u003cabbr title=\"European Union\"\u003eEU\u003c/abbr\u003e, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein by 31 December 2020 and you returned with them to the UK\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethe family member of a British citizen who is also a citizen of an \u003cabbr title=\"European Union\"\u003eEU\u003c/abbr\u003e country, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein, and they lived in the UK as a citizen of one of those countries before becoming a British citizen\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethe child (who is in education in the UK) of someone from the \u003cabbr title=\"European Union\"\u003eEU\u003c/abbr\u003e, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein who used to live and work in the UK\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eYou also cannot use the online service if you’re a primary carer (or the primary carer’s dependant under the age of 18) of:\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ea British citizen (and you did not have another type of permission to stay in the UK)\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ea child of someone from the \u003cabbr title=\"European Union\"\u003eEU\u003c/abbr\u003e, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein who used to live and work in the UK - the child must be in education in the UK\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ea self-sufficient child from the \u003cabbr title=\"European Union\"\u003eEU\u003c/abbr\u003e, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eIf you do not have any of the documents you’ll need to prove your identity, you may not be able to use the online service. \u003ca href=\"/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/what-youll-need-to-apply\"\u003eCheck what you’ll need\u003c/a\u003e before you apply.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003ch3 id=\"if-you-cannot-use-the-online-service\"\u003eIf you cannot use the online service\u003c/h3\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ca href=\"/contact-ukvi-inside-outside-uk\"\u003eContact the \u003cabbr title=\"European Union\"\u003eEU\u003c/abbr\u003e Settlement Scheme team at UK Visas and Immigration\u003c/a\u003e (the ‘Resolution Centre’) to find out how to apply.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eThey will usually send you an application form. You must send your completed application form and supporting documents to the Home Office by post.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cdiv class=\"address\"\u003e\u003cdiv class=\"adr org fn\"\u003e\u003cp\u003e\n\u003cabbr title=\"European Union\"\u003eEU\u003c/abbr\u003e Settlement Scheme\u003cbr\u003ePO Box 2076\u003cbr\u003eLiverpool\u003cbr\u003eL69 3PG\n\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eYou must not send your form back by email unless the Resolution Centre has told you to do so.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eIf you’re \u003ca href=\"/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/family-carer-british-citizen\"\u003eapplying as the family member or primary carer of a British citizen\u003c/a\u003e and you’re eligible to apply, you’ll be given a form with a unique reference number. You must use this form to apply.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eIf you’re not eligible to apply, the Resolution Centre will tell you and you will not be sent a form.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003ch2 id=\"when-you-can-apply-from-outside-the-uk\"\u003eWhen you can apply from outside the UK\u003c/h2\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eIf you’re from the \u003cabbr title=\"European Union\"\u003eEU\u003c/abbr\u003e, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein, you can apply from outside the UK if you hold either a valid passport or national identity card with a biometric chip.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eIf you’re from somewhere else, you can apply to the \u003cabbr title=\"European Union\"\u003eEU\u003c/abbr\u003e Settlement Scheme from outside the UK if you have a UK-issued biometric residence card (BRC). You can use it for 5 years after the expiry date printed on the card.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eOtherwise, you will need to apply for an \u003ca href=\"/family-permit\"\u003e\u003cabbr title=\"European Union\"\u003eEU\u003c/abbr\u003e Settlement Scheme family permit\u003c/a\u003e to come to the UK. Once you’re in the UK you can apply to the \u003cabbr title=\"European Union\"\u003eEU\u003c/abbr\u003e Settlement Scheme.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003ch2 id=\"fees\"\u003eFees\u003c/h2\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eIt’s free to apply to the scheme.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003ch2 id=\"get-help\"\u003eGet help\u003c/h2\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003e\u003ca rel=\"external\" href=\"https://ukvi-euss-support-webchat.homeoffice.gov.uk\"\u003eChat to UK Visas and Immigration (\u003cabbr title=\"UK Visas and Immigration\"\u003eUKVI\u003c/abbr\u003e) using webchat\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eYou can also get help over the phone.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eThe phone number is different if you’re from a local council or another organisation helping others to apply.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n\u003ch3 id=\"if-youre-inside-the-uk\"\u003eIf you’re inside the UK\u003c/h3\u003e\n\n\u003cdiv class=\"contact\"\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eTelephone: 0300 123 7379 \u003cbr\u003e\nMonday to Friday (excluding bank holidays), 8am to 8pm \u003cbr\u003e\nSaturday and Sunday, 9:30am to 4:30pm\u003cbr\u003e\n\u003ca href=\"/call-charges\"\u003eFind out about call charges\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/div\u003e\n\n\u003ch3 id=\"if-youre-outside-the-uk\"\u003eIf you’re outside the UK\u003c/h3\u003e\n\n\u003cdiv class=\"contact\"\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eTelephone: +44 (0)20 3080 0010 \u003cbr\u003e\nMonday to Friday (excluding bank holidays), 8am to 8pm \u003cbr\u003e\nSaturday and Sunday, 9:30am to 4:30pm \u003cbr\u003e\n\u003ca href=\"/call-charges\"\u003eFind out about call charges\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/div\u003e\n\n\u003ch3 id=\"if-youre-from-an-organisation-helping-others-to-apply\"\u003eIf you’re from an organisation helping others to apply\u003c/h3\u003e\n\n\u003cdiv class=\"contact\"\u003e\n\u003cp\u003eTelephone: 0300 790 0566\u003cbr\u003e\nMonday to Friday (excluding bank holidays), 9am to 5pm\u003cbr\u003e\n\u003ca href=\"/call-charges\"\u003eFind out about call charges\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/div\u003e\n\n\u003cp\u003eYou can also \u003ca href=\"/assisted-digital-help-online-applications\"\u003eget support if you need help doing things online\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\n"
}
</script>
