<div class="gem-c-heading govuk-!-margin-bottom-6">

  <h1 class="gem-c-heading__text govuk-heading-xl">
    Apply to the EU Settlement Scheme
</h1></div>

      <div data-module="govspeak" class="gem-c-govspeak gem-c-govspeak--direction-ltr js-disable-youtube govuk-!-margin-bottom-0" data-govspeak-module-started="true">
    
        
        <p>You can apply using any device, for example, a laptop, Android device or iPhone.</p>

<p><a href="/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/what-youll-need-to-apply">Check what you’ll need</a> before you apply.</p>

<p>If you have pre-settled status already, it will be extended by 5 years before it’s due to expire. You’ll be sent an email telling you when this happens.</p>

<p>If you’re eligible, your extended pre-settled status may be automatically converted to settled status or you can apply for settled status. </p>

<p>Find out more about <a href="/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/switch-from-presettled-status-to-settled-status">moving from pre-settled status to settled status</a>.</p>

<h2 id="apply">Apply</h2>

<p>The deadline for applying for most people was 30 June 2021. You can still apply if either:</p>

<ul>
  <li>the deadline for you to apply is after 30 June 2021</li>
  <li>you have <a href="/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/eligibility">‘reasonable grounds’ for why you’re applying now, and not by the deadline or in the time since the deadline passed</a>
</li>
</ul>

<p>If you’re <a href="/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/apply-settled-status-for-child">applying for yourself and your children</a>, make your own application first.</p>

<p><a class="gem-c-button govuk-button govuk-button--start" role="button" data-module="govuk-button" data-ga4-attributes="{"event_name":"navigation","type":"start button"}" draggable="false" href="https://apply-to-visit-or-stay-in-the-uk.homeoffice.gov.uk/euss" data-govuk-button-init="" data-govuk-button-module-started="true"><span> Start now </span><svg class="govuk-button__start-icon govuk-!-display-none-print" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="17.5" height="19" viewBox="0 0 33 40" focusable="false" aria-hidden="true"><path fill="currentColor" d="M0 0h13l20 20-20 20H0l20-20z"></path></svg></a></p>

<p>The Home Office will use the personal information you provide to decide whether to grant your application. Find out <a href="/guidance/eu-settlement-scheme-how-we-use-your-personal-information">how the Home Office will process your personal information</a>.</p>

<h2 id="continue-your-application">Continue your application</h2>

<p>If you’ve already started to apply, you can <a rel="external" href="https://apply-to-visit-or-stay-in-the-uk.homeoffice.gov.uk/dashboard/">continue your application</a>.</p>

<h2 id="who-cannot-use-this-service">Who cannot use this service</h2>

<p>You cannot use the online service to apply to the scheme if you’re applying as:</p>

<ul>
  <li>the family member of a British citizen you lived with in the <abbr title="European Union">EU</abbr>, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein by 31 December 2020 and you returned with them to the UK</li>
  <li>the family member of a British citizen who is also a citizen of an <abbr title="European Union">EU</abbr> country, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein, and they lived in the UK as a citizen of one of those countries before becoming a British citizen</li>
  <li>the child (who is in education in the UK) of someone from the <abbr title="European Union">EU</abbr>, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein who used to live and work in the UK</li>
</ul>

<p>You also cannot use the online service if you’re a primary carer (or the primary carer’s dependant under the age of 18) of:</p>

<ul>
  <li>a British citizen (and you did not have another type of permission to stay in the UK)</li>
  <li>a child of someone from the <abbr title="European Union">EU</abbr>, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein who used to live and work in the UK - the child must be in education in the UK</li>
  <li>a self-sufficient child from the <abbr title="European Union">EU</abbr>, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein</li>
</ul>

<p>If you do not have any of the documents you’ll need to prove your identity, you may not be able to use the online service. <a href="/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/what-youll-need-to-apply">Check what you’ll need</a> before you apply.</p>

<h3 id="if-you-cannot-use-the-online-service">If you cannot use the online service</h3>

<p><a href="/contact-ukvi-inside-outside-uk">Contact the <abbr title="European Union">EU</abbr> Settlement Scheme team at UK Visas and Immigration</a> (the ‘Resolution Centre’) to find out how to apply.</p>

<p>They will usually send you an application form. You must send your completed application form and supporting documents to the Home Office by post.</p>

<div class="address"><div class="adr org fn"><p>
<abbr title="European Union">EU</abbr> Settlement Scheme<br>PO Box 2076<br>Liverpool<br>L69 3PG
</p></div></div>

<p>You must not send your form back by email unless the Resolution Centre has told you to do so.</p>

<p>If you’re <a href="/settled-status-eu-citizens-families/family-carer-british-citizen">applying as the family member or primary carer of a British citizen</a> and you’re eligible to apply, you’ll be given a form with a unique reference number. You must use this form to apply.</p>

<p>If you’re not eligible to apply, the Resolution Centre will tell you and you will not be sent a form.</p>

<h2 id="when-you-can-apply-from-outside-the-uk">When you can apply from outside the UK</h2>

<p>If you’re from the <abbr title="European Union">EU</abbr>, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein, you can apply from outside the UK if you hold either a valid passport or national identity card with a biometric chip.</p>

<p>If you’re from somewhere else, you can apply to the <abbr title="European Union">EU</abbr> Settlement Scheme from outside the UK if you have a UK-issued biometric residence card (BRC). You can use it for 5 years after the expiry date printed on the card.</p>

<p>Otherwise, you will need to apply for an <a href="/family-permit"><abbr title="European Union">EU</abbr> Settlement Scheme family permit</a> to come to the UK. Once you’re in the UK you can apply to the <abbr title="European Union">EU</abbr> Settlement Scheme.</p>

<h2 id="fees">Fees</h2>

<p>It’s free to apply to the scheme.</p>

<h2 id="get-help">Get help</h2>

<p><a rel="external" href="https://ukvi-euss-support-webchat.homeoffice.gov.uk">Chat to UK Visas and Immigration (<abbr title="UK Visas and Immigration">UKVI</abbr>) using webchat</a>.</p>

<p>You can also get help over the phone.</p>

<p>The phone number is different if you’re from a local council or another organisation helping others to apply.</p>

<h3 id="if-youre-inside-the-uk">If you’re inside the UK</h3>

<div class="contact">
<p>Telephone: 0300 123 7379 <br>
Monday to Friday (excluding bank holidays), 8am to 8pm <br>
Saturday and Sunday, 9:30am to 4:30pm<br>
<a href="/call-charges">Find out about call charges</a></p>
</div>

<h3 id="if-youre-outside-the-uk">If you’re outside the UK</h3>

<div class="contact">
<p>Telephone: +44 (0)20 3080 0010 <br>
Monday to Friday (excluding bank holidays), 8am to 8pm <br>
Saturday and Sunday, 9:30am to 4:30pm <br>
<a href="/call-charges">Find out about call charges</a></p>
</div>

<h3 id="if-youre-from-an-organisation-helping-others-to-apply">If you’re from an organisation helping others to apply</h3>

<div class="contact">
<p>Telephone: 0300 790 0566<br>
Monday to Friday (excluding bank holidays), 9am to 5pm<br>
<a href="/call-charges">Find out about call charges</a></p>
</div>

<p>You can also <a href="/assisted-digital-help-online-applications">get support if you need help doing things online</a>.</p>

<h2 class="h2">

                                </h2>
      </div>
                  
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-m-motion-detail field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>The London Assembly is concerned that the quality of London’s universal postal service is under threat following the Chancellor Exchequer’s recent announcement that the Government is to sell its remaining stake in Royal Mail<a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/mayor-assembly/london-assembly/meetings-whole-assembly/motions/defending-londons-postal-service#_ftn1" name="_ftnref1" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; border: 0px; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-family: inherit; vertical-align: baseline; color: rgb(37, 95, 175); text-decoration: none; outline: 0px;" title=""><sup>[12]</sup></a>.  Shortly after this announcement the Government sold half of its remaining 30 per cent share<a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/mayor-assembly/london-assembly/meetings-whole-assembly/motions/defending-londons-postal-service#_ftn2" name="_ftnref2" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; border: 0px; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-family: inherit; vertical-align: baseline; color: rgb(37, 95, 175); text-decoration: none; outline: 0px;" title=""><sup>[13]</sup></a>.</p>
<p>This Assembly believes that the move to fully privatise the service not only represents a bad deal for tax payers but will also potentially reduce scrutiny and transparency in an organisation that has been serving the public interest since the early 1500s<a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/mayor-assembly/london-assembly/meetings-whole-assembly/motions/defending-londons-postal-service#_ftn3" name="_ftnref3" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; border: 0px; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: 1.538em; font-family: inherit; vertical-align: baseline; color: rgb(37, 95, 175); text-decoration: none; outline: 0px;" title="">[14]</a>. These concerns are not merely limited to the delivery of the Royal Mail’s core services, but are also relevant in respect of the availability of affordable housing in London, as the Royal Mail seeks to divest itself of land assets capable of delivering thousands of homes in the capital<a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/mayor-assembly/london-assembly/meetings-whole-assembly/motions/defending-londons-postal-service#_ftn4" name="_ftnref4" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; border: 0px; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: 1.538em; font-family: inherit; vertical-align: baseline; color: rgb(37, 95, 175); text-decoration: none; outline: 0px;" title="">[15]</a>.</p>
<p>The London Assembly calls on the Mayor to defend London’s postal service and ensure Royal Mail’s land assets are used to deliver housing across all tenures in the capital by lobbying the government to conduct an open and transparent cost-benefit analysis of selling the remaining 15% stake in the Royal Mail.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/mayor-assembly/london-assembly/meetings-whole-assembly/motions/defending-londons-postal-service#_ftnref1" name="_ftn1" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; border: 0px; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-family: inherit; vertical-align: baseline; color: rgb(37, 95, 175); text-decoration: none; outline: 0px;" title="">[12]</a> <a href="http://www.ftadviser.com/2015/06/04/investments/economic-indicators/royal-mail-privatisation-top-of-chancellor-s-debt-reduction-sUX0WX8FU59TrIh4OYhmPL/article.html" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; border: 0px; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-family: inherit; vertical-align: baseline; color: rgb(37, 95, 175); text-decoration: none; outline: 0px;">http://www.ftadviser.com/2015/06/04/investments/economic-indicators/royal-mail-privatisation-top-of-chancellor-s-debt-reduction-sUX0WX8FU59TrIh4OYhmPL/article.html</a></p>
<p><a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/mayor-assembly/london-assembly/meetings-whole-assembly/motions/defending-londons-postal-service#_ftnref2" name="_ftn2" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; border: 0px; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-family: inherit; vertical-align: baseline; color: rgb(37, 95, 175); text-decoration: none; outline: 0px;" title="">[13]</a> <a href="http://news.sky.com/story/1499747/govt-sells-its-15-percent-stake-in-royal-mail" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; border: 0px; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-family: inherit; vertical-align: baseline; color: rgb(37, 95, 175); text-decoration: none; outline: 0px;">http://news.sky.com/story/1499747/govt-sells-its-15-percent-stake-in-royal-mail</a></p>
<p><a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/mayor-assembly/london-assembly/meetings-whole-assembly/motions/defending-londons-postal-service#_ftnref3" name="_ftn3" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; border: 0px; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-family: inherit; vertical-align: baseline; color: rgb(37, 95, 175); text-decoration: none; outline: 0px;" title="">[14]</a> <a href="http://www.royalmailgroup.com/Timeline" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; border: 0px; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-family: inherit; vertical-align: baseline; color: rgb(37, 95, 175); text-decoration: none; outline: 0px;">http://www.royalmailgroup.com/Timeline</a></p>
<p><a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/mayor-assembly/london-assembly/meetings-whole-assembly/motions/defending-londons-postal-service#_ftnref4" name="_ftn4" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px; border: 0px; font-style: inherit; font-variant: inherit; font-weight: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: inherit; font-family: inherit; vertical-align: baseline; color: rgb(37, 95, 175); text-decoration: none; outline: 0px;" title="">[15]</a> Julia Kollewe, Royal Mail may reap £662m from planned sale of London sorting office, <em>The Guardian</em>, 11.11.14</p>
</div>

<div class="page-section">

          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h2 class="h2">
                                          Summary of petition
                                </h2>
      </div>
                  
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“Dear Boris Johnson, please hold an official investigation into the behaviour of the Metropolitan Police on Wednesday 4th, Thursday 5th and Friday 6th December against peacefully protesting University of London students.”</p>
</div>
      
  </div>
          </div>
  </div>
    
          

    
<h2 class="h2">
                    Response information
            </h2>
                    <div class="u-mt-5 u-gap-y-4 u-grid u-grid-cols-1 md:u-grid-cols-2 md:u-gap-x-14 lg:u-gap-x-10 xl:u-gap-x-12 xxl:u-gap-x-16">
                                                                    <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Name of person responding:</span>
                  <span>The Mayor</span>
                </p>
                                                        <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Response date:</span>
                  <span>Tuesday 8 April 2014</span>
                </p>
                                    </div>
          
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“Dear Joanne</p>
<p>I write in response to the petition you presented to the Plenary meeting on 5 March about the policing of student protests in central London on 4 and 5 December 2013.</p>
<p>It is my understanding that the events on the 4 and 5 December were part of an ongoing dispute between The University of London Union (ULU) and the University that started in June 2013, and that the vast majority of those protests have passed off peacefully.</p>
<p>It would appear that the nature of that protest changed on 4 and 5 December which necessitated a change in policing response. The MPS is committed to facilitation peaceful protest and to actively engaging with organisers to ensure that this happens. However, where breaches of the peace occur as they did on those two days, the police tactics will rightly change. It is my understanding that on the 4 December, police arrived to deal with a breach of the peace that occurred as security staff were trying to evict students from Senate House and which resulted in furniture being thrown at officers. On the 5 December, it is my understanding that a number of students participating in the protest were armed with homemade flares and shields.</p>
<p>Whatever the circumstances, I police officers to behave professionally and ethically, and I know this is a view that the Commissioner, Sir Bernard Hogan-Howe, shares. I understand that in response to complaints, a Professional Standards is investigation ongoing and I would not like to pre-empt the findings of that.”</p>
</div>

    Meet sales assistant and uni student Mustafe

    Mustafe works as a sales assistant at Currys alongside his university degree.

    1 minute 30 second watch

    View transcript

    My name is Mustafe. I work at Currys as a sales colleague. I've been here for about a year and 3 months, and I do it alongside my university course which is cyber security.

    Make sure all the, you know, aisles are filled up, make sure everything’s looking presentable. Make sure everything’s priced up correctly so all the tags are correct.

    The longer I’ve been here, the more that my skills have actually grown. I think I've built a lot of my problem-solving skills. Being confident in yourself, being able to communicate effectively, and the third thing I’d say is just, you know, being patient, I’d say, being patient with customers, you know, actually getting to know them, building rapport and helping them get the tech they need.

    Knowing that you've personally helped someone with a problem that they've had and you're dealing with not just one customer. There's many customers you’re dealing with throughout the day. It is a job that is quite rewarding in that sense.

    It's never the same thing every day. Even if there's like different customers are coming for the same item. They may have come in for a different reason, and they've lived a different life to the other person. So when you speak to them and you know, you're kind of going through that life journey with them, it's very different each time.

    It's a very like fast-paced environment. So you learn a lot of things through that fast-paced environment, and you build the skills just as fast. So not only is the job interesting, but it's fast-paced, you learn a lot and as well as that, you can build your skills.

    Once you join, you learn about different things. You’re given lots of different opportunities to, you know, progress further on. So it's quite a rewarding job as well. You know, I'd like to continue building on and progressing through the ranks because I really enjoy the job.

          <div aria-hidden="true" class="focus:u-not-sr-only u-sr-only is-hidden section-title">
        

    
<h2 id="in-this-section-56933-title" class="h2">
                                          In this section
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<p><meta charset="utf-8"></p>
<p>This accessibility statement applies to the Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) register site at <a href="https://www.london.gov.uk/what-we-do/environment/pollution-and-air-quality/non-road-mobile-machinery-register/login">https://www.london.gov.uk/what-we-do/environment/pollution-and-air-qual…</a>.</p>
<p>This website is run by the Greater London Authority (GLA). We want as many people as possible to be able to use this website. For example, that means you should be able to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Change colours, contrast levels and fonts</li>
<li>Zoom in up to 400% without the text spilling off the screen and without content being truncated or overlapping</li>
<li>Navigate most of the website using just a keyboard</li>
<li>Navigate most of the website using speech recognition software</li>
<li>Listen to most of the website using a screen reader (including the most recent versions of JAWS, NVDA and VoiceOver)</li>
</ul>
<p>We’ve also made the website text as simple as possible to understand.</p>
<p><a href="https://mcmw.abilitynet.org.uk/">AbilityNet</a> has advice on making your device easier to use if you have a disability.</p>
</div>

  </div>

      </div>

  </div>

    </div>
  </div>

      </div>

<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-py-8 lg:u-py-9 xl:u-py-12 xxl:u-py-14 u-space-y-7">

<h2 id="how-accessible-this-website-is-56935-title" class="h2">
                                          How accessible this website is
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<p>This site has been built to be as accessible as possible and tested against WCAG 2.2 AA. There are some areas which are not yet fully accessible:</p>
<ul>
<li>In all pages there is only one way to locate a specific web page within a set of web page and no other means.</li>
<li>Some form labels that include an asterisk (*) character do not provide instructions to explain that they indicate required fields.</li>
<li>Some labels on forms do not convey that input is mandatory.</li>
<li>Some input fields that collect an individual’s personal data, in the Log in, Register, and Edit profile pages do not have the necessary “autocomplete” attributes.</li>
<li>After an hour, sessions time out and the login page is displayed with no ability to extend or adjust the session.</li>
<li>No instructions are provided to convey that for each row in the "GLA Group" table, on the Contract Machinery Register page, can be operated to display additional details.</li>
<li>Tooltips (Home, Admin, Logout) on some pages cannot be dismissed using any mechanism.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="issues-affecting-people-who-use-keyboard-navigation">Issues affecting people who use keyboard navigation</h3>
<ul>
<li>All the parent menu links (Users, Site Lookups, Machinery Lookups, Retrofit Lookups, Exemption Lookups) do not receive focus and cannot be operated to reveal additional navigation links.</li>
<li>Links within the users table on some pages, do not receive focus and cannot be operated using the keyboard.</li>
<li>It is not possible to tab backwards or forwards in the form within the 'Create new record' modal window.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="issues-affecting-people-with-low-vision">Issues affecting people with low vision</h3>
<ul>
<li>Some combinations of text and background colour do not have sufficient colour contrast.</li>
<li>Some content is lost when the user overrides the setting for spacing between paragraphs, lines, words or characters.</li>
<li>The text and some form controls will not reflow into a single column when you change the size of the browser window on some pages.</li>
<li>Checkboxes on the 'Contract Machinery Register' page and the 'Create new record' modal window on some pages, do not meet the minimum size of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or have sufficient spacing around them to make them easier to operate.</li>
<li>The "Register site" button, on the 'Register a site' page, is truncated in the landscape display but not in the portrait display.</li>
<li>Some buttons (Save, Save and Close, Cancel) and dropdown lists (Role, GLA Group, Borough) are not displayed in portrait display, within the 'Create new record' modal window.</li>
<li>The "Create another (optional)" checkbox receives keyboard focus but does not display any focus indicator.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="issues-affecting-screen-reader-users">Issues affecting screen reader users</h3>
<ul>
<li>Form labels with an asterisk (*) character do not have a text alternative and are not fully accessible to screen reader software.</li>
<li>On most pages the breadcrumb navigation component is not marked up correctly for screen readers.</li>
<li>Status messages in the 'Log in' page, Contract Machinery Register page, Edit profile page, and the Users table component are not read by assistive technologies automatically even though the status message is not in focus.</li>
<li>Some headings on most pages are not marked-up correctly so screen reader users cannot identify the structure of the content.</li>
<li>Some form controls are missing labels and cannot be identified when using a screen reader.</li>
<li>Listboxes, on the 'Contract Machinery Register' page, Register a site page, Create an organization contract page, are not marked up correctly so screen reader users cannot identify them properly.</li>
<li>Page titles on the 'Register a site' page, Create an organization contract page, Edit profile page are too generic and do not properly convey the page.</li>
<li>The correct language of the page is not conveyed programmatically on most pages.</li>
<li>Pagination components are missing labels and cannot be identified when using a screen reader.</li>
<li>The current page in the pagination list is not marked up correctly so screen reader users cannot identify them properly.</li>
<li>The tablist (Personal) component within the 'Create new record' modal window is not marked up correctly so screen reader users cannot identify the structure of it.</li>
<li>Some form controls are missing roles, within the 'Create new record' modal window, so screen readers cannot recognise them.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="issues-affecting-speech-control-users">Issues affecting speech control users</h3>
<ul>
<li>The visible text label "Ok, got it", in the Cookie banner, does not match the match the programmatic label of the component in the code.</li>
</ul>
</div>

<h2 id="technical-information-about-this-websites-accessibility-56945-title" class="h2">
                                          Technical information about this website’s accessibility
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <div class="rich-text">
<p>The Greater London Authority (GLA) is committed to making its website accessible, in accordance with the Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) (No. 2) Accessibility Regulations 2018.</p>
<h3 id="compliance-status">Compliance status</h3>
<p>This website is partially compliant with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines version 2.2 AA standard, due to the non-compliances listed below.</p>
</div>

<div class="page-section">
  <div class="u-py-8 lg:u-py-9 xl:u-py-12 xxl:u-py-14 u-space-y-7">
          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h2 id="non-accessible-content-56947-title" class="h2">
                                          Non accessible content
                                </h2>
      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <div>
<p>The content listed below is non-accessible for the following reasons.</p>
<h3 id="non-compliance-with-the-accessibility-regulations">Non compliance with the accessibility regulations</h3>
<ul>
<li>Form labels with the asterisk (*) character do not have a text alternative and are not fully accessible to screen reader software. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 1.1.1 (non-text content).</li>
<li>On most pages the breadcrumb navigation links are not marked up correctly for screen readers. This fails WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.3.1 (Info and relationships).</li>
<li>Some headings on most pages are not marked-up correctly so screen reader users cannot identify the structure of the content. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 1.3.1 (Info and relationships).</li>
<li>There are no instructions to convey that for each row in the "Machinery awaiting a decision" table, the "Your Sites" table, and the "GLA Group" table can be operated to display additional details in the 'User Dashboard' page and the 'Contract Machinery Register' page. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) Success criterion 1.3.1 (Info and relationships).</li>
<li>Pagination link containers are missing labels and cannot be identified when using a screen reader. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 1.3.1 (Info and relationships).</li>
<li>The current page in the pagination components are not marked up correctly so screen reader users cannot identify them properly. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 1.3.1 (Info and relationships).</li>
<li>All the parent menu links do not receive focus and cannot be operated to reveal additional navigation links. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 2.1.1 (Keyboard).</li>
<li>Links within the users table on some pages, do not receive focus and cannot be operated using the keyboard. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 2.1.1 (Keyboard).</li>
<li>It is not possible to tab backwards or forwards in the form within the 'Create new record' modal window. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 2.1.1 (Keyboard).</li>
<li>After 1 hour the login page is displayed with no ability to extend or adjust the session length. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable).</li>
<li>Page titles on the 'Register a site' page, Create an organization contract page, Edit profile page are too generic and do not properly convey the page. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 2.4.2 (Timing Adjustable).</li>
<li>The visible text label "Ok, got it" in the Cookie banner, does not match the programmatic label of the component in the code. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 2.5.3 (Label in name).</li>
<li>The correct language of the page is not conveyed programmatically on most pages. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 3.1.1 (Language of page).</li>
<li>Some form controls are missing labels and cannot be identified when using a screen reader. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 3.3.2 (Labels or instructions).</li>
<li>There are no instructions to accompany the use of the asterisk (*) symbols in forms. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 3.3.2 (Labels or instructions).</li>
<li>Some form labels that include the asterisk (*) character do not provide instructions to convey that they signify mandatory fields. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 3.3.2 (Labels or instructions) and WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 2.4.6 (Headings and Labels).</li>
<li>Listboxes on the 'Contract Machinery Register' page, Register a site page, Create an organization contract page, are not marked up correctly so screen reader users cannot identify them properly. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 4.1.2 (Name, role and value).</li>
<li>The tablist (Personal) component within the 'Create new record' modal window is not marked up correctly so screen reader users cannot identify the structure of it. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 4.1.2 (Name, role and value).</li>
<li>Some form controls are missing roles within the 'Create new record' modal window, so screen readers cannot recognise them. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level A) success criterion 4.1.2 (Name, role and value).</li>
<li>The "Register site" button, on the 'Register a site' page, is truncated in the landscape display but not in the portrait display. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 1.3.4 (Orientation).</li>
<li>Some buttons (Save, Save and Close, Cancel) and dropdown lists (Role, GLA Group, Borough) are not displayed in portrait display, within the 'Create new record' modal window. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 1.3.4 (Orientation).</li>
<li>Some input fields that collect an individual’s personal data in the Log in, Register, and Edit profile pages, are not coded correctly and do not have the necessary “autocomplete” attributes. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 1.3.5 (Identify input purpose).</li>
<li>Colour contrast issues on certain pages may make it difficult for visually impaired users. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 1.4.3 (Colour contrast) and 1.4.11 (Non-text Contrast).</li>
<li>The text and some form controls will not reflow in a single column when you change the size of the browser window on some pages. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 1.4.10 (Reflow).</li>
<li>Some content is lost when the user overrides the setting for spacing between paragraphs, lines, words or characters. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 1.4.12 (Text spacing).</li>
<li>Tooltips (Home, Admin, Logout) on some pages, cannot be dismissed using any mechanism. This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 1.4.13 (Content on hover or focus).</li>
<li>In all pages there is only one way to locate a specific web page within a set of web page and no other means.This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 2.4.5 (Multiple ways).</li>
<li>The "Create another (optional)" checkbox does not display any focus indicator.This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 2.4.7 (Focus visible).</li>
<li>Checkboxes on the 'Contract Machinery Register' page and the 'Create new record' modal window on some pages, do not meet the minimum size of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or have sufficient spacing around them to make them easier to operate.This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 2.5.8 (Target size).</li>
<li>Status messages in the 'Log in' page, Contract Machinery Register page, Edit profile page, and the Users table component are not read by assistive technologies automatically even though the status message is not in focus.This fails WCAG 2.2 (Level AA) success criterion 4.1.3 (Status message).</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="disproportionate-burden"><strong>Disproportionate burden</strong></h3>
<p>N/A - There are no issues in this category.</p>
<h3 id="content-that-s-not-within-the-scope-of-the-accessibility-regulations">Content that’s not within the scope of the accessibility regulations</h3>
<ul>
<li>The map as provided by Google on the register a site and view site details pages where some features do not have alternate text or are not keyboard selectable.</li>
</ul>
<p>As this is third-party content that is not under our control (neither funded nor developed by us), it falls under the exemptions of the accessibility regulations - Application, 4. (2)(e). However, we have reported this to Google via their feedback form.</p>
</div>

      </div>
            <div class="u-space-y-10">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--rich-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            
<div class="rich-text">
      <div>
<p>This statement was prepared on 04 February 2025. It was last updated on 24 June 2025.</p>

<p>We followed GOV.UK guidance on deciding how to check the Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) register site as follows:</p>

<h2 class="h2">
                                          Summary of petition
                                </h2>
      </div>
                  
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“We don’t want our bus stops in Bromley Market Place and East Street taken away!  We want our buses to continue to serve East Street.  So, we want TfL to stop the present consultation and to come to a community-led planning meeting to improve on the Bromley North Village proposals.”</p>
</div>

                    Response information
            </h2>
                    <div class="u-mt-5 u-gap-y-4 u-grid u-grid-cols-1 md:u-grid-cols-2 md:u-gap-x-14 lg:u-gap-x-10 xl:u-gap-x-12 xxl:u-gap-x-16">
                                                                    <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Name of person responding:</span>
                  <span>The Mayor</span>
                </p>
                                                        <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Response date:</span>
                  <span>Monday 2 December 2013</span>
                </p>
                                    </div>
          
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“Dear Murad</p>
<p>Re: Petitions received at the London Assembly (Plenary) Meeting on 9 October 2013</p>
<p>Thank you for the petition presented to the London Assemble on 9 October. I apologise for the delay, but I asked Transport for London (TfL) to consider the matter thoroughly before responding to you.</p>
<p>As you will be aware, the London Borough of Bromley undertook a consultation for the North Village scheme last year, as I understand it, with broadly positive results. However, because Bromley’s scheme requires significant changes to the bus network, TfL undertook a further consultation specifically on the scheme’s impact on local buses last year. I understand that you would like TfL to attend a community-led planning meeting to discuss the scheme further, and I have therefore asked TfL to get in touch with you to discuss the most appropriate way forward, in tandem with the London Borough of Bromley</p>
<p>Thank you again for writing to me.”</p>
</div>

<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“We call on the Mayor and Transport for London to increase the frequency of the 481 bus service, which currently only runs hourly.”</p>

                    <div class="u-mt-5 u-gap-y-4 u-grid u-grid-cols-1 md:u-grid-cols-2 md:u-gap-x-14 lg:u-gap-x-10 xl:u-gap-x-12 xxl:u-gap-x-16">
                                                                    <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Name of person responding:</span>
                  <span>The Mayor</span>
                </p>
                                                        <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Response date:</span>
                  <span>Tuesday 16 December 2014</span>
                </p>
                                    </div>
          
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>Thank you for the petition you presented at the London Assembly (Plenary) meeting on 5 November calling for Transport for London (TfL) to increase the frequency of its services on bus route 481.</p>
<p>TfL regularly reviews the bus network and feedback from bus users is important to understand changing travel patterns and demands. When making decisions about the development of the bus network, TfL looks at a range of factors such as existing routes, frequency of services, reliability and the ease of interchange. The bus network should be comprehensive, frequent, reliable , and easy to understand and use.</p>
<p>TfL reviewed bus route 481 in 2008 to determine whether there would be sufficient passenger benefit to justify the cost involved with increasing the frequency of the service. Unfortunately, TfL found that there was insufficient demand to justify the cost of increasing the frequency of the service to two buses per hour, which would cost around £221,000. As passenger demand, which is around 700  passenger trips per day, has not grown since 2008, TfL does not have any current plans to change the service."</p>
</div>

<div class="page-section">

          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h2 class="h2">
                                          Summary of petition
                                </h2>
      </div>
                  
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“We the undersigned call upon the Mayor of London to increase the number of bus countdown indicators on Greyhound Lane and Streatham Vale. As the busiest station in Streatham, we believe that Streatham Common Station is under served in terms of information about onward bus travel. This is especially relevant to women and those travelling late at night when they have been advised not to get mobile phones out on leaving the station by the police”.</p>
</div>
      
  </div>
          </div>
  </div>
    
          

    
<h2 class="h2">
                    Response information
            </h2>
                    <div class="u-mt-5 u-gap-y-4 u-grid u-grid-cols-1 md:u-grid-cols-2 md:u-gap-x-14 lg:u-gap-x-10 xl:u-gap-x-12 xxl:u-gap-x-16">
                                                                    <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Name of person responding:</span>
                  <span>The Mayor</span>
                </p>
                                                        <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Response date:</span>
                  <span>Friday 30 January 2015</span>
                </p>
                                    </div>
          
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>Thank you for the petition you presented to the London Assembly (Plenary) meeting on 9 December 2014 about bus arrival information on Greyhound Land and Streatham Vale, and at Streatham Common Station. I apologise for the delay in responding to you.</p>
<p>The successful completion of Transport for London’s (TfL) Countdown II on-street sign upgrade project in July 2012 delivered over 2,500 signs across London. This represents a significant increase from the original estate of around 1,900 signs. For the roll out, all existing Countdown I locations retained the service, while TfL introduced over 600 signs in new locations, agreed with the local boroughs, in sites that maximised benefits to customers.</p>
<p>Since then, the London boroughs have been offered the option of purchasing new signs where they can identify their own, or third-party, funding to support this aim. A review process, managed by TfL, ensures funds are targeted to bus stops that are accessible and include a shelter before they are considered for a sign. More than 30 externally-funded signs have been installed since the introduction of this review process and TfL has ongoing discussions with a number of boroughs for even more signs to be installed.</p>
<p>The Countdown II project also introduced many new ways to access live bus arrival information for all 19,000 bus stops. This includes through personal handsets on TfL’s website or using TfL’s SMS service, as well as through its open data policy, which has enabled hundreds of live travel information apps to be developed. TfL uses advances in technology to ensure more and more customers have access to this information.</p>
<p>‘Digital sign’ subscriptions have also enabled third-parties to display on-screen real-time bus arrival information free of charge at a range of locations, such as shopping centres, schools, libraries and health centres as well as other busy interchange locations. TfL is also working to develop a means of displaying real-time bus arrival information in bus stations. This is currently being trialled at a small number of selected locations and, if successful, could be rolled out across London.</p>
<p>I fully appreciate that your constituents would like to see Countdown signs at these locations. In light of the rapid changes in the way people are accessing this information, TfL has no funding allocated to increase the number of Countdown signs at stops. TfL remains happy to work with all London boroughs to install and connect new signs in locations where third-party funding can be found.</p>
<p>Thank you again for writing to me.</p>
</div>

<h2 class="h2">
                                          Summary of petition
                                </h2>
      </div>
                  
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“We, the undersigned, never want there to be riots in Croydon again. We therefore call upon the Mayor of London, Boris Johnson, to reverse his decision, supported by David Cameron, to cut 1,800 police officers in London over the next three years, and also to drop his plan as Mayor to cut 300 police sergeants from London’s 630 Safer Neighbourhood Teams. We call for an increase in police numbers and local Safer Neighbourhood Teams.”</p>
</div>
      
  </div>

<h2 class="h2">
                    Response information
            </h2>
                    <div class="u-mt-5 u-gap-y-4 u-grid u-grid-cols-1 md:u-grid-cols-2 md:u-gap-x-14 lg:u-gap-x-10 xl:u-gap-x-12 xxl:u-gap-x-16">
                                                                    <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Name of person responding:</span>
                  <span>The Mayor</span>
                </p>
                                                        <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Response date:</span>
                  <span>Friday 25 May 2012</span>
                </p>
                                    </div>
          
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“Dear Val</p>
<p>Thank you for the petition presented to the London Assembly plenary meeting on 7 March about police numbers and local Safer Neighbourhood Teams. I apologise for the delay in responding to you.</p>
<p>I have promised to keep police numbers in London at a safe level, which I have said on numerous occasions is approximately 32,000 warranted officers.</p>
<p>Whilst maintaining police numbers is crucial, I have also ensured that several other mechanisms have been put in place to increase the number of officers available when they are most needed, focusing on increasing the number of special constables available across London, and ensuring that where possible, police officers are patrolling on their own rather than in pairs or groups, thus improving the visibility of officers.</p>
<p>In respect of the reassignment of sager neighbourhood sergeants, you will be aware that I have subsequently announced that I am boosting SNTs by 2000 officers across London. This will more than offset the changes to which you refer.”</p>
</div>

<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“We the undersigned, call upon the Mayor of London to establish a pedestrian crossing and associated road safety features at the junction of the Tulse Hill and Brixton Water Lane, SW2 1DF to improve safety for pedestrians, cyclists and all road users.”</p>

                                                        <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Response date:</span>
                  <span>Wednesday 3 December 2014</span>
                </p>
                                    </div>
          
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>"Thank you for your petition, presented to the London Assembly (Plenary) meeting on 5 November, calling for Transport for London (TfL) to establish a pedestrian crossing and associated road safety features at the junction of Tulse Hill and Brixton Water Lane.</p>
<p>So that you are aware, the London Borough of Lambeth is the HIghway Authority for this junction, and a local major retailer area has offered to make a financial contribution towards the provision of improved pedestrial facilities here.</p>
<p>Both TfL and I fully support this aspiration, and TfL is working closely with the London Borough of Lambeth as well the retailer and their agents towards this.</p>
<p>At the moment, all parties are working towards a solution that adequately balances the needs of all users of the junction, which includes pedestrians. If we can agree a design which achieves this, as well as the required funding to implement the scheme, TfL will deliver these improvements as soon as possible within its existing programme of works."</p>
</div>

<h2 class="h2">
                                          Summary of petition
                                </h2>
      </div>
                  
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“We the residents living in Roehampton Vale are strongly concerned about the safety for pedestrians and motorists using the pavement on Roehampton Vale often competing with cyclists. Cyclists are unsafe to cycle on the main road with speedy 40mph motorists; that’s why they are cycling on the narrow pavement, competing dangerously with pedestrians, motorist stopping in an emergency and Kingston University students at the bus stop.  We consider it will be much safer and the risk of accidents will be reduced if the speed limit between Robin Hood Gate and Tibbets Corner is reduced from 40 to 30mph.  We request the support of Wandsworth Council and the Mayor of London in reducing the speed limit to 30 miles per hour.”</p>
</div>
      
  </div>
          </div>
  </div>
    
          

    
<h2 class="h2">
                    Response information
            </h2>
                    <div class="u-mt-5 u-gap-y-4 u-grid u-grid-cols-1 md:u-grid-cols-2 md:u-gap-x-14 lg:u-gap-x-10 xl:u-gap-x-12 xxl:u-gap-x-16">
                                                                    <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Name of person responding:</span>
                  <span>The Mayor</span>
                </p>
                                                        <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Response date:</span>
                  <span>Monday 3 November 2014</span>
                </p>
                                    </div>
          
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>"Thank you for your letter of 11 September about the petition presented by Richard Tracey AM to the London Assembly on 10 September. I apologise for the delay in responding to you. I understand your also wrote to Sir Peter Hendy about this matter and I enclose a copy of his response. As Sir Peter mentioned in his reply, Transport for London (TfL) and I remain firmly committed to improving conditions for pedestrians and cyclists. My ambitious programme of, among other things, cycling infrastructure improvements is now underway and will generally look for opportunities to provide a higher degree of segregation for cyclists on carriageways.</p>
<p>Many sections of the TfL Road Network away from central London, where cyclist and pedestrian numbers are low, have shared footway areas. This is the case, for example, along Roehampton Vale. While I fully appreciate the local concerns that have been raised in the petition, at this time, TfL considers this to be the best option for this section of the A3 as it carefully balances the needs of the various users of this corridor.</p>
<p>Turning to the suggestion in the petition to reduce the speed limit between Robin Hood Gate and Tibbets Corner, TfL has discussed this with the Metropolitan Police Service and they have concluded that 40mph is an appropriate speed limit for this dual carriageway section of the A3. It is also line with national guidance on this issue.</p>
<p>Thank you"</p>
</div>

      <p>If you use assistive technology (such as a screen reader) and need a version of a PDF or other document on this page in a more accessible format, please get in touch via our <a data-entity-substitution="canonical" data-entity-type="node" data-entity-uuid="709bb75e-8985-4a4f-a823-d88109c9f5e8" href="/contact-us-form" title="Contact us form">online form</a> and tell us which format you need.</p>

<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“We the residents living in Roehampton Vale are strongly concerned about the safety for pedestrians and motorists using the pavement on Roehampton Vale often competing with cyclists. Cyclists are unsafe to cycle on the main road with speedy 40mph motorists; that’s why they are cycling on the narrow pavement, competing dangerously with pedestrians, motorist stopping in an emergency and Kingston University students at the bus stop.  We consider it will be much safer and the risk of accidents will be reduced if the speed limit between Robin Hood Gate and Tibbets Corner is reduced from 40 to 30mph.  We request the support of Wandsworth Council and the Mayor of London in reducing the speed limit to 30 miles per hour.”</p>

<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>"Thank you for your letter of 11 September about the petition presented by Richard Tracey AM to the London Assembly on 10 September. I apologise for the delay in responding to you. I understand your also wrote to Sir Peter Hendy about this matter and I enclose a copy of his response. As Sir Peter mentioned in his reply, Tranport for London (TfL) and I remain firmly committed to improving conditionsfor pedestrians and cyclists. My ambitious programme of, among other things, cycling infrastructure improvements is now underway and will generally look for opportunities to provide a higher degree of segregation for cyclists on carriageways.</p>
<p>Many sections of the TfL Road Network away from central London, where cyclist and pedestrian numbers are low, have shared footway areas. This is the case, for example, along Roehampton Vale. While I fully appreciate the local concerns that have been raised in the petition, at this time, TfL considers this to be the best option for this section of the A3 as it carefully balances the needs of the various users of this corridor.</p>
<p>Turning to the suggestion in the petition to reduce the speed limit between Robin Hood Gate and Tibbets Corner, TfL has discussed this with the Metropolitan Police Service and they have concluded that 40mph is an appropriate speed limit for this dual carriageway section of the A3. It is also line with national guidance on this issue.</p>
<p>Thank you"</p>

                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Response date:</span>
                  <span>Monday 8 September 2014</span>
                </p>
                                    </div>
          
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>"Thank you for your petition presented by Caroline Pidgeon to the London Assembly plenary meeting on 16 July. I apologise for the delay in responding to you.</p>
<p>The shelter at Highbury Grange bus stop was unfortunately damaged following a road traffic collision on February this year. Prior to its replacement, Transport for London had to ensure that the replacement was located appropriately in order that it did not fall victim to a similar incident. On 13 June, TfL installed a new shelter slightly further away from the kerb to mitigate the risk of a further vehicle strike.</p>
<p>I trust this fully addresses the concerns raised.</p>
<p>Thank you again for writing to me.</p>
<p>Yours ever"</p>
</div>

<h2 class="h2">
                                          Summary of petition
                                </h2>
      </div>
                  
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>We are concerned at the loss of 194 police officers in Southwark since 2010 and call on the Mayor of London to restore our lost officers.</p>
</div>
      
  </div>

  </div>
    
          

    
<h2 class="h2">
                    Response information
            </h2>
                    <div class="u-mt-5 u-gap-y-4 u-grid u-grid-cols-1 md:u-grid-cols-2 md:u-gap-x-14 lg:u-gap-x-10 xl:u-gap-x-12 xxl:u-gap-x-16">
                                                                    <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Name of person responding:</span>
                  <span>The Mayor</span>
                </p>
                                                        <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Response date:</span>
                  <span>Friday 6 February 2015</span>
                </p>
                                    </div>
          
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>Thank you for the petition presented to the London Assembly plenary meeting on (9 December 2014) about police officer numbers in Southwark. I apologise for the delay in responding to you.</p>
<p>It is simply not true that Southwark has lost 194 officers since 2010.</p>
<p>I am committed to maintaining police officer numbers. Unlike other parts of the country, the Metropolitan Police Service (MPS) is in the midst of a major recruitment drive – hiring 5,000 new police officers so we can keep numbers at around 32,000. Furthermore, these police officers are being moved to the front line where they are needed most – there will be an extra 2,600 officers in neighbourhoods by April 2015.</p>
<p>The way that borough policing is structured has changed over the last few years. A number of officers who were previously counted under the command of the Borough Commander now report centrally, although they still undertake borough duties. For example, officers in Intelligence and Custody are now under centralised command. This has impacted on some of Southwark’s officers who have been centralised in this way, however they continue to work in the borough and provide a service to Southwark’s communities.</p>
<p> Taking account of this centralisation, the current 2015 target for Southwark is 760 officers. Southwark currently has 763 officers, including 13 in training.</p>
<p>Although there have been changes to the overall number of borough officers the commitment to increase local safer neighbourhood teams remains. The decision to put an extra 2,600 officers in neighbourhoods means that we have been able to commit to increasing the number in Southwark from 62 in 2011 to 178 by 2015.</p>
<p>This increase of 116 is the second highest in London and I understand that all of these officers are now in place.</p>
<p>Thank you again for writing.</p>
</div>

<h2 class="h2">

                                </h2>
      </div>
                  
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“We the undersigned request Transport for London, as the responsible Highway Authority, to implement further measures to control vehicle speeds along Clapham Common Westside from the junction with The Avenue to Battersea Rise; in particular the installation of 30mph flashing lights close to the Bowood Road junction and surface treatment of the carriageway to alert motorists”</p>

<h2 class="h2">
                    Response information
            </h2>
                    <div class="u-mt-5 u-gap-y-4 u-grid u-grid-cols-1 md:u-grid-cols-2 md:u-gap-x-14 lg:u-gap-x-10 xl:u-gap-x-12 xxl:u-gap-x-16">
                                                                    <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Name of person responding:</span>
                  <span>The Mayor</span>
                </p>
                                                        <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Response date:</span>
                  <span>Monday 7 April 2014</span>
                </p>
                                    </div>
          
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“Dear Roger</p>
<p>Re: Petitions received at the London Assembly (Plenary) Meeting on 5 March 2014</p>
<p>Thank you for the petition which you submitted to the London Assembly on 5 March requesting the introduction of further speed control measures along Clapham Common West Side between The Avenue and Battersea Rise.</p>
<p>As you may be aware, Transport for London (TfL) conducted work on Clapham Common West Side last year following reports of infrastructure damage, especially near the two consecutive bends between Grandison Road and Battersea Rise, and safety concerns raised by local residents. As part of this work a speed survey was undertaken which showed that 85 per cent of vehicles observed were travelling at speeds of 29mph or lower.</p>
<p>In order to improve drivers’ awareness of the road layout and deter the minority of motorists speeding through the area, TfL introduced a range of new measures on Clapham Common West Side last December. These included new surface treatment to the carriageway, “SLOW” markings, virtual speed cushions and improved chevron signage. TfL believed that the combination of these measures will be effective in alerting motorists to the road alignment and curb speeding through the area. TfL intends to undertake follow up speed surveys in the near future. Clearly, if this shows continued problems we will need to consider what further measures may be needed.</p>
<p>Turning to the petition’s suggestion to introduce “flashing 30mph signs”, or speed indicator devices as they are known, I can confirm that TfL has not introduced such signs in recent years. This decision was based on evidence collected with indicates that such features have little lasting impact on driver behaviour and, therefore, represent poor value for money.</p>
<p>I can assure you TfL has taken the concerns of local residents seriously and introduced a number of measures to address the issues that have been raised. However, a review of the collision data for the section indicates that over the past three years there were four collisions in total and, following their investigations, the police confirmed that none of these collisions was caused by speeding vehicles.”</p>
</div>

<div class="page-section">

          <div class="section-title">
        

    
<h2 class="h2">
                                          Summary of petition
                                </h2>
      </div>
                  
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>“We the undersigned express our dismay at the scheme to convert Premier House from business premises into flats. More than 100 businesses, charities and other organisations are set lose their premises and hundreds of local jobs are at risk. This move is an economic and social double whammy for Edgware, as many other Edgware businesses themselves depend on those who work in Premier House for their own trade. We are surprised that Barnet Council did not obtain an exemption from the relaxation of the planning rules that have caused this to happen and call upon the Council, even at this late stage, to apply immediately to the Government for such an exemption. We call on the Council and the London Mayor to work with those based in Premier House facing eviction to try to avert this economic catastrophe, and if the businesses are not permitted to remain, to assist them in every possible way to relocate locally.”</p>
</div>
      
  </div>
          </div>
  </div>
    
          

    
<h2 class="h2">
                    Response information
            </h2>
                    <div class="u-mt-5 u-gap-y-4 u-grid u-grid-cols-1 md:u-grid-cols-2 md:u-gap-x-14 lg:u-gap-x-10 xl:u-gap-x-12 xxl:u-gap-x-16">
                                                                    <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Name of person responding:</span>
                  <span>The Mayor</span>
                </p>
                                                        <p class="u-text-sm xl:u-text-lg xxl:u-text-xl">
                  <span class="u-font-bold"> Response date:</span>
                  <span>Monday 15 December 2014</span>
                </p>
                                    </div>
          
<div class="rich-text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-c-pt-response-details field--type-text-long field--label-hidden field__item"><p>"Thank you for the petition you presented to the London Assembly (Plenary) Meeting on 5 November about the proposed residential led mixed-use development at 102-124 Station Road, Edgware.</p>
<p>I considered an initial consultation report (reference D&P/3176/YP) on this proposal on 19 March 2014, which I have enclosed for your information. In this report I raised a number of strategic concerns that were required to be addressed by the applicant. I was subsequently advised by Barnet Council on 12 May 2014 that members had resolved to refuse permission for the proposed development on 1 May 2014.</p>
<p>The application was referred back to me following the committee decision, where it was subsequently assessed by officers, taking account of the issues raised within the committee report, our initial consultation report and all representations received. I considered a report detailing the findings of this assessment on 29 May 2014 where, whilst I raised no concerns regarding the principal of the proposal, I did raise a number of strategic concerns that were required to be addressed by the applicant.</p>
<p>My recommendation was that Barnet Council be advised that I am content for it to determine the case itself, subject to any action that the Secretary of State may take, and I do not therefore wish to direct refusal or direct that I am to be the local planning authority. I enclose a copy of this report (reference D&P/3176/02) for your information. In reaching this decision I had due regard to the concerns raised within the petition, as well as the detailed assessment of the proposals by my planning officers. I have sent a copy of this letter to the Leader of Barnet Council."</p>
</div>
